From: Samira Khan <samira.k@novamed.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Partial 503s and truncated responses from hosted inference

Hi Lauren —

We're seeing intermittent 503s and short/truncated outputs from the hosted inference API starting around 08:50 PT this morning. About ~7% of calls to /v1/generate return a 503 and a handful of responses are cut off mid-sentence. Our ingest pipeline retries, but that adds latency spikes and a couple of duplicate user outputs.

Examples attached (harvester_log_20261129.txt) and a quick curl example:
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rwd-stable-1","prompt":"Summarize..."}'
-> HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable (payload id: f3a1)

Can your team confirm whether this is a region-level issue or something on our side? We have a high-traffic batch running until 11:00 PT and would appreciate visibility.

Thanks,
Samira
Director, Platform Engineering — NovaMed

[Attachment: harvester_log_20261129.txt (text, 120KB)]

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@novamed.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2026 09:25:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Partial 503s and truncated responses from hosted inference

Hi Samira —

Thanks for the heads up and for the log — sorry for the disruption. We're seeing a matched signal in our telemetry for p95/p99 elevation and a small fraction of 503s originating from the us-west-2 pool. We've opened an incident internally and published a brief notice on our status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-11-29-partial-503s.

Immediate actions we're taking (ETA in comments):
- Ops is throttling a small set of recently-deployed prefetch workers to reduce fanout (ben, see below). (ETA 10m)
- We're enabling an extra routing pool to offload traffic from impacted hosts. (ETA 25-35m)
- Prefix cache snapshots collected for root-cause (attached).

Can you confirm whether NovaMed can tolerate the transient retries (we'll avoid aggressive retries on our side) or if you want us to enable a temporary canary that pins you to a dedicated pool? If you prefer the dedicated path we'll prioritize the allocation.

I'll keep this thread updated; cc'ing Ben for the ops playbook and Evelyn for post-incident comms.

—Lauren
Principal Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: prefix_cache_snapshot_11-29.json (json, 2.1MB)]

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, Samira Khan <samira.k@novamed.com>
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2026 10:00:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Partial 503s and truncated responses from hosted inference

Hi all —

Quick ops update from the runbook: we observed a surge in outbound prefetch fanout combined with an uneven KV cache eviction pattern on a subset of us-west-2 inference hosts. Root cause looks tied to a recent prefetch tuning change rolled last night. Steps executed:

1) Scaled down the prefetch concurrency on the impacted lane (rolled back the tuning). Impact: immediate reduction in 503 rate from ~7% -> ~1.5% (observed over 6m).
2) Activated secondary routing pool for pinned customer traffic; NovaMed traffic has been steered to the new pool as of 09:48 PT.
3) Purged a stale prefix cache segment and collected diagnostics into S3 (link: s3://redwood-incident-logs/2026/11/29/).

We're continuing to monitor; next steps: full traffic redistribution and a blocklist for the specific prefetch commit pending RCA. I'll post an ops bridge summary to the Jira ticket INF-4827 in the next hour.

Attachments: harvester_log_20261129.txt (truncated extract attached below).

ben
Senior Site Reliability Engineer — Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2026 15:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Incident update and next steps — mitigation complete, postmortem timeline

Samira —

Follow-up: ops has completed redistribution and the 503 rate has returned to baseline (<0.1% over the last 2 hours). We've annotated the status page with a mitigation entry and set the incident to "under investigation": https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-11-29-partial-503s.

What to expect next:
- RCA (root cause analysis) draft to be shared by EOD tomorrow (2026-11-30). It will include the timeline, the specific prefetch tuning delta that regressed cache pressure, and the list of commits blocked pending rollback.
- A follow-up change window where we'll validate a guarded rollout for the prefetch tuning with NovaMed on a dedicated pool (if you opt-in).
- A discretionary invoice credit offer for customer impact windows (we'll coordinate with your procurement contact if you'd like to take that up).

If you prefer to be pinned to a dedicated pool for a week as a precaution, say the word and we'll prioritize allocation. Also sharing the Jira link with detailed logs: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/INF-4827.

Appreciate your patience — we'll keep the channel open and notify when the RCA is published.

Best,
Lauren
Principal Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference
